back:
x1 = (σ2² − σ1 σ2 ρ) / (σ1² + σ2² − 2 σ1 σ2 ρ),   x2 = 1 − x1

Use: The lowest-risk combination of two stocks.
Trap: Expected returns play no role.

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.

x1 = σ2 / (σ1 + σ2)  →  σp = 0

Use: Perfectly negatively correlated assets.
Trap: Special case ρ = 0: x_1 = σ_2² / (σ_1² + σ_2²).

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.

front: Formula: Mixing with the risk-free asset (CAL)
back:
E(R) = rf + x (E(RP) − rf)
σ = x σP

Use: Lending (0 < x < 1) or borrowing (x > 1) combined with a risky portfolio P.
Trap: Leverage scales premium and risk in the same proportion – the Sharpe ratio stays.

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.

SP = (E(RP) − rf) / σP

Use: Ranking risky portfolios when you can borrow and lend at r_f.
Trap: Positive Sharpe = beats r_f in expectation; it says nothing about 'above one'.

front: Formula: Hitting a target risk or return
back:
target σ:  x = σtarget / σT
target return:  x = (Etarget − rf) / (E(RT) − rf)

Use: Beat a given portfolio with the tangency (or market) portfolio.
Trap: x > 1 means borrowing (negative risk-free weight).

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.
